pure-announcement.rationale: This is third-party coverage of a disclosed attack technique with a published proof of concept, not a product launch or release note.

duplicate.rationale: No nearest concept touches multimodal prompt injection, poisoned convention files, or supply-chain attacks on coding agents; the closest (siem-agentic-visibility-gap) is about SIEM logging, not this attack class.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The claims trace to the ASSET Research Group's linked disclosure page and an open-source PoC repo with the split-payload PR and decoder, which a reader can inspect and reproduce.

durability.rationale: The attack-class mechanisms — instructions hidden in an image channel text-diff reviewers never parse, secrets exfiltrated as non-string-shaped integer tuples, deferred activation through a merged convention file, and outcomes depending on harness more than model — remain exploitable patterns long after the specific tool/model results (Cursor, Sonnet 4.6, GPT-5.5) go stale.

actionability.rationale: It names the exact blind spots a defender must close — CodeRabbit's default PNG exclusion, text-only diff review, string-pattern secret scanning, and unvetted AGENTS.md instructions — which directly changes how someone configures AI code review and treats repo convention files.

atomicity.rationale: The note is one attack pattern — split-payload multimodal prompt injection into coding agents via repository convention files — with the harness-vs-model result and the detector prototype as supporting findings of the same study.
